transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-05 16:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Platform: Zoom (recording available)
- Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (EmberLynx), Jonah Kim (EmberLynx), Priya Sharma (EmberLynx)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Redwood and EmberLynx did an exploratory compatibility scan for integrating Redwood's private/dedicated inference into EmberLynx's SaaS onramp. Key topics: GPU selection & availability, VPC/private control plane, KMS/encryption, SSO & audit logs, latency vs cost tradeoffs, pilot success criteria and next steps to run a benchmark.

Topics: hybrid onramp patterns, VPC peering, GPU SKUs, SOC2/KMS, autoscaling policies, model variants fallback

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect)
00:00 Avery: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood inference, i'm the AE on this side and with me is Samir our solutions eng, Samir say hi
00:10 Samir: hey hi all, happy to be here, i'll be the technical lead on the convo, can dig into runtime and GPU questions
00:18 Marta: thanks, yeah from EmberLynx i'm marta, head of platform, we run a multi-tenant SaaS that does code analysis for finance clients, we're evaluating options to offload llm inferencing to a partner onramp model
00:30 Jonah: jonah here, CTO, i'll be looking at cost and roadmap fit and making the call in jan if pilot looks good
00:38 Priya: priya, lead SRE, i'll own network/security/ops bits and the pilot run
00:45 Avery: great quick agenda: compatibility scan — where you are today, constraints, what Redwood can offer (hosted/dedicated/private), typical pilots, and open q's. also we can share a short deck and a benchmark template after this
01:03 Marta: perfect, we'll try to be concise, wanted to start with our current stack — we run k8s EKS, mixed a100 and t4 workloads, models are mostly open LLMs fine-tuned in house, sensitive PII redaction requirements, and we need audit logs retained for 2 years for a couple clients
01:25 Samir: okay EKS + A100s t4 mix, good, do you currently run batching in inference path or is it request-per-user?
01:32 Marta: currently synchronous per-request, we tried naive batching but it increased latency spikes and clients complained
01:40 Samir: understood, Redwood supports continuous batching with latency SLOs — you can configure a latency-first policy vs cost-first. there is also prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts which can reduce token costs
01:52 Jonah: latency-first sounds interesting; what's the delta versus our current single-request path, ballpark?
01:58 Samir: depends on prompt lengths and model, but for a typical 256 token window we see p95 in dedicated setups around 150-220ms for Llama-derived models on a100x8 style configs, with tiled KV and batching optimized, in hosted may be slightly higher, 250-350ms — numbers rough, we can run a tailored benchmark
02:20 Jonah: hmm that's promising, our SLO is 300ms p95 for critical flows, cost can't be 4x current though, we have to be realistic
02:29 Avery: fair, that's why pilots are useful. we can show tradeoff scenarios — quantized model variants reduce cost a lot, dedicated buckets with autoscale give predictability without blowing up egress/costs
02:41 Priya: security: we need VPC isolation, customer-managed KMS, SAML SSO, and audit logs. Your hosted offering supports some of that?
02:52 Samir: hosted has encryption at rest, but for full isolation and CMK we recommend Redwood Private (VPC), which is the same control plane but deployed to your VPC. it supports KMS/HSM integrations, SSO via SAML, and per-token audit events — there are some ops dependencies to stitch into your network team
03:10 Priya: ok, good. on the network side we have strict egress rules, we prefer VPC peering or private link, no public endpoints for model inferences
03:20 Samir: we can do VPC peering or private link depending on cloud provider; we'll need your VPC CIDRs and peering approach, and possibly a small NAT for outbound updates — we'll document this in the runbook
03:34 Marta: what about data residency? some of our EU clients require EU-only processing
03:39 Avery: Redwood has region-aware deployments; we can pin inference to eu-west or customers' own on-prem clusters in an upcoming private package. for regulated workloads we recommend private with region pinning
03:50 Jonah: on GPUs, we saw a note about quantized variants — would redwood run quantized kernels on a100 or is that mostly for t4/ampere?
03:59 Samir: quantized kernels available across multiple architectures; the benefit depends on model topology and sequence length. we run optimized kernels and choose them at runtime — for some workloads int8 gives similar quality at 2-3x perf/cost improvement. again pilot to measure quality delta on your prompts
04:15 Marta: we want to avoid regression — how do you measure quality and rollback?
04:20 Samir: Redwood Optimize ties model and quantization recommendations to evals — you upload a prompt set, we measure ROUGE/semantic similarity/LLM-specific eval metrics and flag regressions. rollouts support canary & auto-fallback to previous variant on regressions
04:36 Jonah: good, that's necessary. ok can we talk about integration tasks? what does the POC look like operationally?
04:44 Avery: typical POC is 4-6 weeks: week 1 infra prep (VPC, peering, keys), week 2 benchmark run and sample traffic, week 3 tuning (batching+cache), week 4 evaluation + cost analysis and playbook. shorter pilots are possible if you already have infra ready
05:02 Priya: timeline wise we have internal approvals in Jan, but we can start prep in Dec if we lock scope this month
05:09 Marta: yes we want to run pilot before end of jan, decisions after that
05:14 Samir: great, from a technical checklist we'll need sample model artifacts (or model names + weights), sample prompt set (we prefer 200-500 varied prompts), and a small infra contact to coordinate peering and IAM
05:28 Priya: i'll share a network diagram and a list of SGs and VPCs, probably tomorrow
05:36 Jonah: who owns the pilot costs? how are dedicated buckets priced?
05:41 Avery: there are options: usage-based hosted pilot (pay-as-you-go), or a small reserved dedicated bucket for the pilot with a short-term commitment; we'll send both pricing templates. most partners prefer reserved pilot capacity for predictable latency
05:55 Marta: are there hidden fees? storage for KV cache, or data transfer costs?
06:00 Samir: KV cache uses ephemeral storage but we can configure retention; egress is standard cloud egress — with private peering egress cross-region costs may apply. we'll annotate costs clearly in the pricing sheet
06:14 Jonah: competitor question — we've also looked at CloudNova and GigaCompute, they offer a managed onramp but their observability was weak. what's Redwood's observability story?
06:25 Avery: Redwood Console gives per-route token breakdowns, per-model latency percentiles, tracing hooks, and regression alerts tied to your eval sets. plus token-level cost attributions. we can demo a console in a follow-up if useful
06:39 Priya: for security review we'll need SOC2 docs and a pen test summary and clarity on where logs are stored — can you share a redactable copy?
06:48 Avery: yes we'll send SOC2 documentation and an operations runbook. for pen-tests we have a summary and can provide details under NDA if needed
06:57 Samir: small technical note — if you plan to run large KV caches we recommend a dedicated SSD-backed KV node topology to avoid warm-up latency. that is part of our tuning playbook
07:12 Marta: hmm, that matters. our workload has repeated prefix prompts so KV helps a lot. what about model routing and fallbacks if capacity is constrained?
07:22 Samir: smart routing policies route by latency, cost, and region. if dedicated tiers are saturated we can fallback to a compatible quantized or hosted variant, and you can set auto-fallback thresholds
07:34 Jonah: ok good. are there any constraints on bringing our own models (BYOM)?
07:39 Samir: BYOM supported; we onboard model artifacts, validate operators, and test kernels. some proprietary layers or custom ops need a build step. we usually ask for a container or wheel + test harness
07:52 Priya: we have custom CUDA ops for a preprocessing pipeline, would that be a blocker?
07:57 Samir: could be — we'll need to test them in a staging build. if ops are closed-source we can run them in your VPC using Redwood Private so code doesn't leave your environment
08:08 Marta: ok that gives us options. can you run a short sample benchmark next week? we're mostly interested in p95 for 128-512 token replies and cost per 1k tokens
08:20 Avery: yes we'll propose a benchmark plan: 1) run baseline on your infra (if you want), 2) run Redwood private pinned to region, 3) run quantized variant — compare p95 and cost/1k tokens; we'll provide a spreadsheet for results
08:35 Jonah: great. small note: for procurement we might need to see EULA, data processing addendum, and pricing for 12-month reserved capacity — can you early-share those?
08:46 Avery: yep we'll attach EULA/DPA template and a sample reserved contract to the follow-up email
08:52 Priya: on automation, can we define autoscaling policies by queue depth or token per second?
08:58 Samir: yes autoscaling policies support CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, and token throughput. and you can define burst windows for traffic spikes
09:10 Marta: any gotchas on k8s-side when integrating?
09:14 Samir: nothing major, but if you're using sidecars for routing be mindful of grpc vs http2 timeouts — we'll share recommended container settings. also we provide a small agent for metrics collection that can be deployed as a DaemonSet
09:30 Jonah: okay, that sounds reasonable. I have one question about SLA — what uptime or latency SLAs are available on dedicated vs hosted?
09:39 Avery: dedicated comes with SLA-backed targets for throughput and latency tiers as part of enterprise contracts; hosted has best-effort SLAs with credits for outages. we'll include SLA matrix in the pricing packet
09:52 Priya: can we do a short security call with your compliance lead earlier than the full legal review? a 30-min intro to validate basic red flags
09:59 Avery: absolutely, i'll make the intro, target email by monday
10:05 Marta: ok wrapping up — this was useful. any other open technical risks?
10:11 Samir: main ones: custom CUDA ops, network peering timing, and quantization quality for your specific prompts. all mitigable via pilot
10:21 Jonah: agreed. sounds like we can proceed with scope: 4-week pilot, private VPC deployment, quantized vs full accuracy runs, run the benchmark week of Dec 14.
10:33 Avery: i'll follow up with the deck and benchmark template and we'll coordinate calendar invites for the prep kick-off.
10:40 Marta: thanks everyone, we'll look for the email and send the network docs
10:44 Priya: thanks, bye
10:45 Meeting end (recording saved)
